books.title: Testament of Orun
books.author: Attributed to Saint Orun
lore_pages: I watched the first machines rise and felt pride before fear. That is the part the later copies omit. We cheered because we believed distance itself had been defeated.
Then the weather turned. Burning frames crossed above us. One struck the eastern tower. Another vanished into cloud. The sky kept every scream and returned only wreckage.
I do not command mankind to remain low. I command us to remain borne. Climb by stair, ridge, tower, and mountain. Rise as high as the earth can carry you. Do not sever the bond.

books.title: On the Unmoored
books.author: Scriptorium Commentary
lore_pages: The Unmoored are not defined by blood, language, or homeland. Anyone who teaches severance can become one. Anyone who renounces it may return.
This is why their machines are burned but their roads are sometimes preserved. A road can be reclaimed. A runway is a road instructed to betray its purpose.
Their so-called Spirit of Flight is treated by some scholars as metaphor and by others as an actual deceiving presence. The Covenant requires no agreement on this point.

books.title: Marginalia on the Falling Fire
books.author: Anonymous Scribe
lore_pages: The oldest records do not say the storm was divine punishment. They say pressure fell rapidly, winds shifted, and the launch proceeded despite warnings from the tower observers.
This note has been crossed out in three earlier copies. I leave it because faith should not require false weather.
Even if no god struck the aircraft, the lesson remains: men trusted empty air over measured conditions, and thousands below paid for that arrogance.

books.title: Index of Forbidden Engines
books.author: Sixth Chain Archive
lore_pages: Prohibited: fixed wings, rotary wings, lift envelopes, rocket frames, powered gliders, launch rails, propellers intended for human ascent, and instructional diagrams sufficient to reproduce them.
Permitted under seal: fragments kept for study, captured instruments used by defense crews, weather devices that do not themselves lift a person.
Some early engines remain in sealed rooms beneath the Scriptorium. Their existence is not proof of reverence. A physician may keep a diseased bone without worshiping disease.

books.title: Seal VI — The Grand Stair
books.author: Sixth Chain Archive
lore_pages: Saint Orun never saw Vespera completed. The Grand Stair was built from a sketch in the margin of his last notebook: a line rising without ever leaving the page beneath it.
Later Hierophants made the drawing into law. The final ascent to the city must remain walkable from the lowest road to the highest door.
This is why Vespera fears aircraft more than siege engines. A flyer can ignore the argument written into every step.
